summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, asthma, and a history of multiple suicide attempts was admitted after being found unresponsive in her car following a drug overdose involving clonidine, haloperidol, and olanzapine. She presented with a GCS of 8, bradycardia, and respiratory depression requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. Initial labs showed an elevated lactate and anion gap metabolic acidosis, both of which resolved with fluid resuscitation. CT head showed no acute intracranial abnormalities. She developed a prolonged QT interval, likely due to the overdose and bradycardia, which improved with supportive care and electrolyte repletion. She was extubated without complications and regained full mental clarity. Phlebitis at an IV site was noted but remained mild. Psychiatry recommended continuation of lithium therapy. She was medically stabilized and transferred to a psychiatric facility for ongoing care.
problems: Bipolar I disorder, most recent episode (or current) depressed, unspecified
Suicide and self-inflicted poisoning by tranquilizers and other psychotropic agents
Phlebitis and thrombophlebitis of superficial veins of upper extremities
